title: Trump: Bomb threats target Democratic strongholds on Election Day
description_short: Trump: Bomb threats target Democratic strongholds on Election Day
description_medium: On Election Day, November 5, 2024, bomb threats targeted polling and ballot-counting locations in at least five battleground states. NBC News found that most identified sites were in Democratic-leaning counties. Officials considered the threats noncredible, yet some polling places closed temporarily while authorities assessed them. The sender remained unknown.
description_long: Bomb threats were reported at polling places and ballot-counting sites in at least five battleground states on Election Day, November 5, 2024. NBC News compiled 67 locations across 19 counties from local reports and statements by election officials; 56 locations were in 11 counties that had voted for Joe Biden in 2020. Officials did not consider the threats credible, but some polling places were temporarily shut while authorities responded. That temporary closure is a documented disruption; the available report does not say that ballots were lost or that voting results changed. The source reported that some messages appeared to come from Russian email domains, but said it was not clear who sent them. A Russian-looking address does not establish the sender’s identity or a connection to a government, campaign, or candidate. The record supports a wave of threats aimed largely at Democratic-leaning areas, along with temporary interruptions at some sites. It does not establish that Donald Trump directed or knew about the threats, despite the framing that they supported his candidacy.
notes: NBC News reports at least 67 locations, temporary closures at some polling places, and that none of the threats were deemed credible. It says the sender was unknown; the report does not connect the threats to Trump.
revision_reason: Corrected the medium summary to meet the minimum length while retaining the source’s uncertainty and documented disruptions.
